internal.reason: Hand-crafted shader counterpart: that tutorial wires the Nishita sky manually in the Shader Editor; this one scripts the same node graph via bpy. Together they show both authoring paths for the same technique.
The World node tree is the first requirement for EEVEE irradiance baking — the probe system samples the world for background irradiance. Set up the world rig here, then bake probes there.
The Mist pass configured by configure_mist() feeds directly into that compositor workflow — the Z-depth fog and defocus post-process share the same distance envelope.
The reverse pipeline: that tutorial renders a 360° equirectangular HDRI from a scene; the result can be loaded back into ShaderNodeTexEnvironment here to close the loop.
The custom render engine in that tutorial triggers via F12 and exports a GLB — the world rig here provides the lighting context that engine inherits for any EEVEE-baked emission passes.
